methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building outside metro hubs, creating potential peer learning networks that could distribute deep AI fluency beyond traditional tech corridors.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free grassroots AI workshops targeting the technology gap signal bottom-up capability distribution, though sustainability depends on whether shallow platform adoption or deeper skill-building takes hold.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA reinforces Richmond as a secondary hub for deep AI capability, but the metro-institutional model may concentrate expertise rather than distribute it regionally.

signals.title: NoVa lawmakers take AI cash while residents resist data centers - opensecrets.org
signals.signal_reading: Lawmakers taking AI industry cash while residents resist data centers reveals the concentration paradox: NoVA captures AI infrastructure investment but community resistance may limit how that translates to broad-based capability.

signals.title: Column: AI is reshaping Hampton Roads before our eyes - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Commentary on AI reshaping Hampton Roads suggests visible platform-layer adoption across sectors, but without specifics on depth of capability development versus surface-level tool consumption.
